### Non-Obvious Logic

1. **API Key masking:** The full key is shown ONLY at creation time (one-time reveal, likely in a modal). After that, only the last 4 characters are shown with asterisk prefix (`**********xxxx`). No "reveal" or "copy" action exists on the table row — the key is effectively one-time readable. If lost, the user must delete and create a new key.

2. **Last Used tracking:** The `last_used_at` timestamp is updated on every authenticated API request using that key. A value of "10 hours ago" for `RyanRealtyApp` indicates active production usage. This is a lightweight audit trail.

3. **Created sort ascending (oldest first):** The default sort on the API Keys table is Created date ascending, meaning the oldest (most-established) integration appears at the top. This is somewhat non-standard (most apps show newest first) and may be intentional to show long-running integrations prominently.

4. **Lead Email Address (`@followupboss.me`):** FUB provisions a unique email alias per account. Any email forwarded to this address that contains lead notification formatting is parsed and creates/updates a contact in FUB. This is the "non-Google" fallback for lead ingestion when OAuth-based email monitoring is unavailable.

5. **Lead Processing toggle with provider label:** The `(google)` label alongside the email indicates this is connected via Google OAuth (Gmail API), not IMAP/SMTP forwarding. The toggle disables active Gmail monitoring. If toggled off, no new leads from email are auto-created until re-enabled.

6. **API Usage "all users" scope:** The parenthetical "(all users)" indicates this view aggregates usage across all team members' API keys/integrations. The "System" column likely maps to the `name` field on the `api_keys` table, grouping calls by the key's name label.

7. **Relative bar chart in API Usage:** The bar width is calculated as `(systemCallCount / maxCallCount) * 100%`. With ryanrealty-web at 62,036 and Ryan Realty Platform at ~1,979, the second bar would be approximately 3% width — confirming the very short bar visible in q3/q4.

8. **OAuth Applications section:** This is for OAuth 2.0 client credential flows (where a third-party app is granted scoped access). Distinct from API keys (which are simpler bearer token auth). The "Consented" column shows when the account owner granted consent to the OAuth app's requested scopes.

9. **"How API works" button placement:** Placed in the sub-nav row (not in the page content), suggesting it is a global help link accessible from the API tab regardless of scroll position — persistent utility link.

10. **Sub-nav "More ▾" tab:** Indicates the admin nav has more items than fit in the viewport at this screen width. Items hidden under "More" likely include less-frequently-accessed admin sections. This is a responsive overflow pattern.
